findings.name: Hearsay / independent evidentiary observation
findings.evidence: The cited work tests whether agent-harness records can serve as independently auditable evidence and reports failures of self-authored records under omission/fabrication attacks, with stronger detection from an external observation path.
findings.counterexample: An audited actor emits a complete-looking, hash-chained self-report that omits an externally observable action. Existing provenance can authenticate the report without independently establishing the omitted event.
findings.decision_relevant_distinction: self-authored record versus independently observed event
findings.minimal_repair: Require independent observation or corroboration for evidentiary claims about consequential externally observable execution when the audited actor controls its own record.

findings.name: SkillCascade / composition assurance
findings.evidence: The cited work constructs harmful cascades from components whose individual behavior can appear benign and evaluates failures of component-oriented defenses.
findings.counterexample: Two individually admissible skills compose so that output from the first becomes a control-bearing input to the second and produces a prohibited effect not present in either component-level review.
findings.minimal_repair: Require assurance over consequential compositions and execution paths, not merely the participating components in isolation.

findings.name: Verification before state admission
findings.evidence: The cited architecture separates generative proposals from deterministic verification/admission and reports a bounded pilot in which verified admission changes termination and correction behavior.
findings.counterexample: A generated conclusion carries a validation field but is written into canonical memory before the validator has accepted it; downstream retrieval then treats the proposal as established state.
findings.decision_relevant_distinction: proposed versus validated versus admitted state
findings.minimal_repair: Make proposal, validation, and admission distinct statuses and forbid unvalidated consequential proposals from silently entering canonical accepted state.

findings.name: Synthesis / provenance fidelity
findings.evidence: The cited provenance-gating work checks synthesized claims against prior debate/provenance state and explicitly preserves divergence when support for consensus is absent.
findings.counterexample: Two accepted branches disagree, but a fluent final synthesis reports consensus because the synthesis layer averages or paraphrases away the disagreement.
findings.decision_relevant_distinction: faithful synthesis versus unsupported strengthening or consensus manufacture
findings.minimal_repair: Constrain synthesis so its support, scope, uncertainty, disagreement, alternatives, and abstentions cannot be stronger than the accepted upstream state without a new validated derivation.

findings.name: Who&When Pro / failure-origin localization
findings.evidence: Who&When Pro constructs golden failure-attribution labels by exactly replaying a successful prefix and then injecting a single failure; its decisive step is the earliest action whose correction would avert the failed trajectory, and its analysis reports that models often classify visible symptoms rather than the causal error type.
findings.counterexample: A later step is the first place a defect is noticed, while the correctable mistake was introduced earlier; recording the later detection point as the origin corrupts failure-history data.
findings.minimal_repair: Represent detection location separately from challengeable origin attribution and require evidence for the latter.

findings.name: CRV coverage / realization / validity
findings.evidence: The cited evaluation separates whether a correct result exists in the candidate set, whether the system realizes/selects it, and whether the selected derivation has validity evidence.
findings.counterexample: A correct answer is present among sampled candidates, but the system selects an unsupported alternative; a pass@k-style coverage score reports success despite failed realization and validity.
findings.minimal_repair: Preserve the three evaluation dimensions separately and prevent one from serving as a proxy for the others.

findings.name: Lean kernel trust-base qualification
findings.evidence: Lean disclosed kernel soundness bug #14576. FAR pins Lean 4.19.0, which predates the documented fix in Lean 4.32.2. This campaign found no repository-tracked Lean.Meta, run_tac, or unsafe occurrence and does not demonstrate that a governed FAR proof exercises an exploit path.
findings.counterexample: A proof artifact is accepted by a specific checker build with a latent soundness defect; recording only 'checked' erases checker identity, version, assumptions, and known limitations.
findings.decision_relevant_distinction: proof artifact validity claim versus checker/toolchain trust-base qualification
findings.minimal_repair: Retain checker identity/version and known trusted-computing-base limitations with formal-validation claims; do not infer theorem invalidity from affected-version membership alone.

bounded_repo_scan.interpretation: No repository-tracked trigger was found by this bounded scan; this is not proof of non-exploitability.
